function.arguments: {"observation": "The `patient_id` column has 48 duplicate values, meaning some patients appear more than once in the dataset. According to the data dictionary, this is because 24 patients were re-tested (i.e., re-assayed), and each re-test appears as a separate row with `sample_seq = 1` and `sample_seq = 2`. The data dictionary states that the row with the highest `sample_seq` supersedes earlier rows for that patient.", "implication": "If we compute the mean baseline biomarker value across all rows, we would be double-counting 24 patients (once for each test), which would bias the mean if the two measurements differ. To compute a per-patient mean, we must deduplicate the data by keeping only the row with the highest `sample_seq` for each patient. This changes the analysis: we must deduplicate before computing the mean."}
function.name: note_finding
